item.title: SonicWall SMA 8200v Cross-Parameter Blind SQL Injection to Root (CVE-2026-4112)
item.description:

Affected Target

Field Value
Software / System SonicWall SMA 8200v management console (Jetty + Struts 2, port 8443)
Versions Affected Firmware 12.5.0-02283 confirmed; likely all 12.x
Language / Platform Python 3 PoC against a Java (Struts 2) web management console
Authentication Required Yes (any valid management console credential, including read-only accounts)
Network Access Required Yes

Summary

The SonicWall SMA 8200v management console contains a post-authentication blind SQL injection in the /activeUsers.action endpoint, reachable by any authenticated user regardless of role — including a read-only monitoring account. The application’s safeParam() sanitizer escapes quotes but not backslashes, so a trailing backslash in the realmFilter parameter escapes the closing quote the application appends, letting the adjacent communityFilter parameter inject arbitrary SQL across the string-literal boundary. Because the backing MariaDB account (DbAdmin) holds the FILE privilege and LOAD_FILE() reads are not blocked by secure_file_priv=NULL, the injection is used to blind-extract the appliance’s avconfig.xml configuration file character-by-character via time-based (SLEEP) conditions, recovering the primary administrator’s SHA-512 crypt password hash. Since SonicWall uses the same credential for both the console admin and the underlying OS root account, cracking this hash yields full root access to the appliance — turning a low-privilege read-only login into complete device takeover.
